## 5.3. Source maps Node inspector DevTools workflow and flags

### 1) **Source maps — `//# sourceMappingURL=` and Node `--enable-source-maps` / `SourceMap` support**

**Definition** — a *source map* is JSON (`{version:3, sources, mappings}`) mapping generated code (transpiled/bundled `dist/app.js:1:12345`) back to original (`src/app.ts:42:7`). The host loads it via trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=app.js.map` or `data:application/json;base64,…` inline.

**Modern guidance** — emit `sourceMap: true` in `tsconfig.json` / `esbuild`/`vite` config. For Node stack traces from transpiled code, run `node --enable-source-maps app.js`; without it, `stack` points at `dist:1:12345` and triage is blind. In browsers, DevTools loads maps automatically when `sourceMappingURL` is present.

```js
console.log("//# sourceMappingURL=app.js.map");
// Minified example — without map:
function m(a,b){return a+b} // real original: src/math.ts: export const add = (a,b) => a+b
try { m(null.x); } catch(e){ console.log(e.stack.split("\n")[1].slice(0,60)); } // points at m:1:??

// Generated source map JSON shape (illustrative):
const fakeMap = {
  version: 3,
  sources: ["src/app.ts"],
  mappings: "AAAA,SAAS,CAAC",
  sourcesContent: ["export const add = (a:number,b:number)=> a+b;"],
};
console.log("map version", fakeMap.version, "sources", fakeMap.sources);

// Node --enable-source-maps demo — guarded:
// Without flag: stack shows built file line 1; with flag: maps to src/app.ts:42
console.log("run: node --enable-source-maps dist/app.js  // then throw and read mapped stack");
console.log("Node 20+ flag also remaps prepareStackTrace CallSite.getFileName()");

// Inline vs external — inline bloats file, external is separate fetch:
// //# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64,ey...
console.log("bundler inline for dev, external for prod (cacheable)");
```

### 2) **Node inspector — `node --inspect`/`--inspect-brk`, `chrome://inspect`, `vscode` attach, `node:inspector`**

**Definition** — V8 inspector protocol (`--inspect[=host:port]`) exposes debugging via WebSocket. `node --inspect-brk` breaks before first line. Clients: Chrome `chrome://inspect`, `vscode` `launch.json` attach, `ndb`, `node --watch` + inspector.

**Modern guidance** — triage production with logs + stacks; debug locally via inspector. `await` + `debugger` pause needs inspector attached; CI should not use `--inspect`.

```js
console.log("node --inspect app.js  # open chrome://inspect > Open dedicated DevTools");
console.log("node --inspect-brk app.js  # break before first line");
console.log("node --inspect=0.0.0.0:9229 --enable-source-maps app.js");

// Programmatic inspector API — trigger break from code
const inspector = require("node:inspector");
console.log("inspector url:", inspector.url() ?? "not attached");
if (!inspector.url()) console.log("use: inspector.open(9229, '127.0.0.1', true) to enable");

// Example — open, then waitForDebugger
// inspector.open(0); // 0 = random port
// inspector.waitForDebugger(); // pause until client attaches
// console.log("attached — debugger statements now pause");
console.log("close:", typeof inspector.close);

// Signal — `kill -SIGUSR1 <pid>` toggles inspector on running Node
console.log("kill -SIGUSR1", process.pid, " # toggles inspector on running process");

// Guard: --inspect in prod exposes debugger port — never bind 0.0.0.0 publicly
console.log("prod guard: --inspect only on localhost; firewall 9229; strip in Docker prod");

// VS Code launch.json snippet (illustrative):
console.log(JSON.stringify({ type:"node", request:"launch", name:"Attach", runtimeArgs:["--enable-source-maps"] }));
```

### 3) **DevTools workflow — breakpoints vs `debugger`, `logpoints`, `blackbox`, `XHR/fetch` breakpoints, Node `--watch` and `--trace-warnings`**

**Definition** — DevTools workflow: *breakpoint* (pause at `file:line`), *conditional breakpoint* (`expr` guard), *logpoint* (`console.log` without pause), *blackbox/ignoreList* (skip `node_modules`), *XHR/fetch breakpoint* (pause on request), *event listener breakpoint*; Node flags `--trace-warnings`/`--trace-deprecation` show stacks for `process.emitWarning`.

| Tool | Pauses? | Ships to prod? | When |
|------|---------|----------------|------|
| `debugger;` | when attached | if left in source | reproducing with inspector |
| Breakpoint (UI) | always when set | never | local triage, no source edit |
| Conditional BP (`x > 10`) | when expr true | never | tight loop hit few times |
| Logpoint (`console.log(x)`) | no pause | never | observe without stopping |
| Blackbox / ignoreList | skips | no | skip lib frames to focus |
| `--trace-warnings`/`--trace-deprecation` | logs stack per warning | no | trace `process.emitWarning` source |

```js
console.log("DevTools Sources > + Add breakpoint > right-click > Edit breakpoint > x > 10");
console.log("DevTools Sources > logpoint: {console.log('x', x)}");
console.log("DevTools > Settings > Ignore List > add **/node_modules/**");

// Node --trace-warnings demo
process.emitWarning("something deprecated", { code: "DEP0155", type: "DeprecationWarning" });
console.log("run: node --trace-warnings app.js  # shows stack of emitWarning call");
console.log("run: node --trace-deprecation app.js  # same for deprecations");
console.log("run: node --watch app.js  # restart on file change (dev inner loop)");

// Async stack with --async-stack-traces + --enable-source-maps:
console.log("run: node --enable-source-maps --async-stack-traces app.js  # best async triage");

// Example — logpoint via inspector protocol (programmatic):
console.log("inspector Session > Debugger.setBreakpoint, Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl with condition");
```

### 4) **Common confusion**

- "`--enable-source-maps` is on by default" — it is not; Node requires the flag (until a future default) and `ts-node`/`tsx` need their own map setup.
- "`--inspect` is safe in prod behind firewall" — the port gives full control (evaluate arbitrary code) — treat as RCE vector; never expose to internet; use `--inspect` on localhost only via tunnel.
- "`debugger;` is stripped in prod builds" — not unless minifier `drop_debugger: true` (terser/esbuild) is set; lint and strip explicitly.
- "`console.trace` needs inspector" — it does not; it prints to `stderr` synchronously without pausing — use for snapshot triage.

### 5) **Performance note**

Inspector `console.log` when not attached is buffered; excessive logging without consumption still allocates strings. `--enable-source-maps` caches map parsing — one map per file, negligible unless 1000+ chunks. `--trace-warnings` prints per `emitWarning` — avoid in prod hot path; gate with `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`.

### 6) **Mentor note**

Have juniors demonstrate mapping: throw from `dist/app.js:1:12345` without flag (unmappable) vs `node --enable-source-maps` (maps to `src/app.ts:42`). In review, flag `--inspect` on public interfaces and require `sourceMap: true` for any transpiled/bundled service; require `--trace-warnings` when a deprecation warning lacks a stack.
